events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: The Note

options.text: There’s no need for this to come between us!

events.text: After claiming our new City Site we have received a simple note from [character], it reads: “I will remember this.”

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Too Close for Comfort

options.text: Let us recompense [rival] for this slight.
We will settle where we like.

events.text: The messenger reaches you in the dead of night, bringing word of a tense standoff at our newly claimed City Site. [rival] soldiers have been harassing your own, insisting that they had already laid claim to the land. The hastily summoned court suggests that it may be wise to send a gift of appeasement to [character], unless souring relations with his nation is part of your plan.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Too Close for Comfort

options.text: Let us recompense [rival] for this slight.
We will settle where we like.

events.text: [rival] is furious with us over the claim of our latest City Site, a site they had been in the process of settling themselves. A [rival] emissary has arrived to demand that we offer them tribute in compensation. [rival] troops have been seen in the area, but it’s unclear if [rival] is willing to fight over this.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Too Close for Comfort

options.text: Let us recompense [rival] for this slight.
We will settle where we like.

events.text: Claiming our newest City Site seems to have upset [rival]. They claim to have been in the process of settling the same area, but we beat them to it. Some advisors think we should smooth things over with a gift, but an equal number feel that [rival] should have been faster to settle the site if they wanted it so badly. How shall we respond?
